notes: §1985:VI.6.4.4 SR2: "The maximum size of each operand is 18 decimal digits" and the composite of the operands each statement specifies "must not contain more than 18 decimal digits". The per-operand bound is EditionContext.CheckDigitCapacity (COBOL0802 for a 19-digit PICTURE 9(19), an edited Z(18)9 and a 19-digit literal at 85); the composite is StatementValidation.CheckComposite at Edition.MaxDigits = 18, with the per-verb membership the ArithmeticBinder Bind* members pass (all operands for ADD/SUBTRACT format 1, GIVING excluded in format 2, receivers only for MULTIPLY/DIVIDE below 2002 via CompositeMembers.ReceivingItems85, REMAINDER excluded) and CorrespondingBinder.CorrMatch per pair. Probes at --std 85: ADD 9(10) TO V9(9), a COMP S9(10), a P-scaled 9(10)P(5) with V9(4), and an ODO element OT(1) all refused COBOL0805 at 19 and accepted at 18; DIVIDE I9 INTO I10 F9 refused, DIVIDE ... GIVING I9 REMAINDER F9 accepted; CORRESPONDING accepted when only the whole statement spans 19; 2002/2023 accept the same 19-digit composites. Witness: ADD 9(18) TO V9, refused COBOL0805.

next.reason: 1985 VI.6.4.4 (2): 'The maximum size of each operand is 18 decimal digits' and the composite of operands of ADD/DIVIDE/MULTIPLY/SUBTRACT 'must not contain more than 18 decimal digits'. §2023:14.7.7 SR2 limits the composite to 31 digits, only 'when native arithmetic is in effect', excluding intrinsic-function, binary-char..binary-double, float and floating-point-literal operands from it; the composite is defined per statement by §2023:14.9.2.3 SR1, §2023:14.9.12.3 SR4, §2023:14.9.26.3 SR4 and §2023:14.9.44.3 SR1; the per-operand bound is the general digit limit of §2023:13.18.40.3 SR14 ('shall range from 1 through 31'). Every conforming 1985 program is still accepted with the same meaning, but 2023 accepts operands and composites of 19-31 digits that 1985 refuses: a compile-time relaxation, no exception condition.
